1.explanation: The root of the bug is in ComboBox.render(), where the map over filtered items assigns key={itemToString(item)} (and similarly for ItemToElement). When two items share the same display text, itemToString returns identical keys, causing duplicate-key warnings. To fix this, the key prop should prefer the unique item.id (e.g. key={item.id != null ? item.id : itemToString(item)}) to guarantee uniqueness.
1.bug_scenario: In the ComboBox playground the developer passed two items with identical “text” but different “id”. Because ComboBox’s render method uses itemToString(item) to generate the React “key” for each <ListBox.MenuItem> (and for any custom ItemToElement), both items resolve to the same key (“Option”), triggering React’s “duplicate key” warning and potentially incorrect behavior.

2.explanation: Inside the ComboBox’s render method, when mapping over items to produce <ListBox.MenuItem> elements, the code sets the React key to `itemToString(item)` (i.e. the item’s text). If two items share the same text, they get identical keys, triggering React warnings and potentially unstable updates. To fix this, the key should prioritize the item’s unique `id` (e.g. `key={item.id != null ? item.id : itemToString(item)}`) so that each menu item always has a unique key.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a React ComboBox with two items both labeled “Option” (but with different `id` values) rendered in the dropdown. In the browser console there is a warning: “Encountered two children with the same key, ‘Option’.” This happens because the component is using the text returned by `itemToString` as the React key for each `ListBox.MenuItem`, so identical labels produce duplicate keys.
